name: Bhavishyavani Future Soundz
blurb: Mumbai collective whose founders included Ashim Ahluwalia, Mukul Deora and Tejas Mangeshkar; parties from 13 May 1999.

name: Bronski Beat
blurb: Jimmy Somerville, Steve Bronski and Larry Steinbachek, whose 1984 hit "Smalltown Boy" reached number three in Britain.

name: Detroit Techno Militia
blurb: Street-level Detroit DJ-and-producer collective "dedicated to preserving the legacy of true Detroit electronic music": T.Linder, DJ Seoul, Darkcube, Neil V, DJ Psycho, J.Garcia. Label launched 2007; the DTM 5x5 (five DJs, five turntables, 2007); Detroit Music Award 2010; the Made in Detroit stage at Movement 2011; The Grid radio show (2013). Since 2023 a regular guest in Hastings.

name: Drug checking in Zürich (Streetwork and DIZ)
blurb: The city's mobile drug checking from 2001 and fixed testing at the Drogeninformationszentrum from 2006; a stand at the Street Parade.

name: Good Night Out Campaign
blurb: Campaign begun by Hollaback London in March 2014 that trains and accredits venues to deal with sexual harassment.

name: ID&T
blurb: Dutch promoter of Thunderdome and Mysteryland, co-founded by Duncan Stutterheim; sold to SFX in 2013 and to Superstruct in 2021.

name: Killasan
blurb: Osaka reggae sound system crew; a quarter of its club system, shipped to Berlin about 2001, became the centre of the Wax Treatment parties.

name: Major League DJz
blurb: Twins Banele and Bandile Mbere, whose rooftop Balcony Mix streams spread amapiano in lockdown; sold out O2 Academy Brixton in 2022.

name: Moroko Loko
blurb: Amine K's underground party series, started in 2009 against the clubs' commercial music, later holding poolside parties in Marrakech.

name: Papi Juice
blurb: Party and art collective founded by Oscar Nñ and Adam Rhodes for queer and transgender people of colour; first night held in a 72-person bar.

name: Quando Quango
blurb: Factory Records dance group formed by Hillegonda Rietveld and Mike Pickering; "Love Tempo" (1983) was remixed in New York.

name: Saffron
blurb: Bristol label and training project founded by Laura Lewis-Paul, teaching production and DJing to women and gender non-conforming people.

name: Adam Smith and Marcus Lyall
blurb: Show directors of the Chemical Brothers since 2009; Smith has made the duo's visuals since their first gig in 1995.

name: Superjane
blurb: Chicago collective of DJ Heather, Colette, Lady D and Dayhota, who say they were America's first all-woman DJ group.

name: Tuff Jam
blurb: DJ and production duo Matt Jam Lamont and Karl Tuff Enuff Brown, Kiss presenters from 1997 to 2000 and central figures in underground garage.

name: A Club Called Rhonda
blurb: House and disco night begun by Loren Granic and Gregory Alexander, which grew from Guatelinda to Los Globos with a mixed, queer-friendly crowd.

name: Afterlife
blurb: Tale Of Us's melodic-techno party and label: Space in 2016, Privilege in 2017, then Thursdays at Hï Ibiza from 2018, built around big-screen visuals.

name: A.R.T. at Yellow
blurb: K.U.D.O.'s Friday at Yellow in Tokyo, renamed Zero from 1994.

name: Atlas Electronic
blurb: Karim Mrabti's festival at Villa Janna, capped at 2,000 a day, mixing club DJs with gnawa and desert bands.

name: AWOL
blurb: A Way of Life at the Paradise Club, jungle's home.

name: Bass Culture
blurb: D'Julz's monthly residency at the Rex Club from 1997, the longest-standing in the club's history; it marked twenty years in 2017 and played the old room's last party on 27 May 2023.

blurb: Chicago's dance shop on North Clark Street: Derrick Carter and Mark Farina behind the counter.

name: Idle Hands
blurb: Bristol's shop and label on City Road, by Stokes Croft; dubstep's and techno's counter in the 2010s.

name: Lighthouse Records
blurb: Deep house, techno and disco shop opened in Shibuya in 2008, by 2025 in a basement in Kanda-Surugadai.

name: Manhattan Records
blurb: Founded behind Shibuya police station in 1980; its move to Udagawacho in 1992 or 1993 drew the import shops that made the district.

name: Pure Groove
blurb: The UK garage counter where the two-step white labels went first, from a Camden stall in 1988 to Holloway Road and then Smithfield.

name: Rock and Soul
blurb: Midtown record and DJ-equipment shop opened by Shirley and Joseph Bechor in 1975 at 462 Seventh Avenue; now on West 37th Street.
q: "Rock and Soul" New York record shop

name: Rush Hour
blurb: Amsterdam's shop, label and distributor; the Dutch techno and house counter since 1997.

name: Spin Inn
blurb: Manchester's import shop on Cross Street, which supplied the Chicago and New York records Mike Pickering played at the Haçienda.

name: Underground Solu'shn
blurb: Dance shop at 9 Cockburn Street, Edinburgh, started by three DJs and still selling twelve-inches and DJ equipment in 2026.

name: Vinyl Mania
blurb: Carmine Street: Larry Levan's record shop, where Garage records went on sale the Monday after he played them.

name: Alan Fierstein and Acoustilog
blurb: Acoustician who tuned the Paradise Garage with Richard Long and designed its four-way crossover to Acoustilog's specification.

name: Capital Sound
blurb: Hire company that flew 76 Martin Audio F2 cabinets and 54 Amcron amplifiers for Fantazia's Big Bang in 1993.

name: Desert Storm Sound System
blurb: Glasgow free party rig born in after-hours parties during the 1991 Gulf War; it took techno to Tuzla and Sarajevo with aid convoys in 1994–96.

name: Duke Vin the Tickler's
blurb: Vincent Forbes's Ladbroke Grove sound, built in 1955 around a £4 amplifier; by BBC News's 2009 report, thought to be the first sound system at Notting Hill Carnival.

name: Kirsch Audio
blurb: Felix Kirsch's loudspeaker firm in Neukölln, Berlin, known for sound reinforcement and studio monitors.

name: Metro (Percival Miller)
blurb: Valve-amplifier builder for Jah Shaka, Jah Tubby's and others, working from north London on 807 and KT88 valves.

name: Saxon Studio International
blurb: Lewisham sound of Musclehead Francis and Denis Rowe; Papa Levi, Tippa Irie, Smiley Culture and fast chat, spread on cassette.

name: The Spiral Tribe rig
blurb: Spiral Tribe's sound system, bought in 1991: one of the Castlemorton rigs, impounded by police in 1992, then taken to Paris and Berlin as the teknival began.

name: Valve Sound System
blurb: Dillinja and Lemon D's drum and bass rig, a '96K' system that needed three trucks on tour.

name: Dance FM
blurb: Walthamstow's house and rave pirate of 1989–91 on 93.0 FM, set up by Mike Stone to sound like a legal station.

name: Essential Mix
blurb: BBC Radio 1's weekly two-hour guest mix, devised by producer Eddie Gordon and presented by Pete Tong since the first show on 30 October 1993.

name: Pulse FM
blurb: A hardcore pirate of early-1990s London on 90.6 FM, one of the rave-era stations that followed the acid house pirates.
